message.content:
**The 56 signers of the United States Declaration of Independence**

The Declaration was adopted by the Continental Congress on **July 4, 1776** and the signatures were affixed on **August 2, 1776**. The signers were delegates from the thirteen colonies who had been elected to the Congress. Below is the full list of those who signed, grouped by colony:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, James Smith, George Taylor |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, Joseph Warren, John Adams, Paul Revere, John Hancock (again), John Hancock (again) – *Note: John Hancock’s signature is famously large; he is listed once but his name appears prominently on the document.* |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll (the younger) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, John Rutledge |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Nelson Jr., Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton |
| **New York** | Philip Livingston, Francis Lewis, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

### Quick facts

- **Total signers:** 56
- **First signer (by order of appearance):** John Hancock (his large signature is the most recognizable)
- **Last signer (by order of appearance):** Roger Williams (Rhode Island)
- **Notable facts:**  
  - **Benjamin Franklin** was the only signer who was not a delegate to the Continental Congress; he was a delegate to the Congress of the Confederation and signed the Treaty of Paris in 1783.  
  - **John Hancock** is famous for signing the Declaration with a large, bold signature, which has become a symbol of the act of signing itself.  
  - **Charles Carroll of Carrollton** was the only Catholic signer.  
  - **George Washington** did not sign the Declaration because he was not a delegate to the Continental Congress; he was the commander-in-chief of the Continental Army.

These individuals represented the collective decision of the colonies to break away from British rule and form a new nation.
